D6E2.Settings.SecondEdition.Options.seco: Additional Skill modules
Each optional Skill module adds 2D to the character-creation Skill budget (Second Edition p. 20). Enter only modules actually used by this campaign.
Use Skill Specialization & Advanced Skills
Enable the optional Advanced Skill and Specialization structures from Second Edition pp. 96-99.
Use Module: Perks, Flaws & Talents
Enable native Second Edition feature creation accounting and typed feature services (pp. 101-129).
Use Module: Troubles & Assets
Enable Trouble and Asset invocation, Hero Point transactions, and GM-owned twice-per-session resets (pp. 130-131).
Use Module: Pips
Enable +1 and +2 Die Code modifiers, split-die character creation, and sequential pip advancement (Second Edition pp. 94-95). Core Second Edition otherwise uses whole dice.
Use Module: Chases
Enable the scene-persistent opposed chase tracker with Distance, capture, escape, and Exceptional Success shifts (Second Edition pp. 73-74).
Use Module: Environments
Enable GM-authoritative cold, heat, poisonous-air, and drowning checks with persistent printed effects (Second Edition pp. 77-78).
Use Module: No Dodge Defense
Replace personal ranged Dodge defenses with the printed point-blank, short, medium, long, and long-range-dodging difficulties while retaining Parry (Second Edition p. 94).
Remove Stunned
Remove the Stunned level and make Wounded the first normal damage level (Second Edition p. 89).
Remove Wounded
Remove the Wounded level, making Stunned the first normal damage level and Mortally Wounded the next (Second Edition p. 89).
Use Killing Blows
A personal target dies immediately when Brawn resistance totals less than half Damage; one Hero Point may be spent to survive (Second Edition p. 90).
Cap Brawn + Armor at 6D
Cap personal Brawn-plus-Armor resistance pools at 6D before rolling; relative Scale remains a separate modifier (Second Edition p. 90).
Equipment era
Select one campaign equipment family from Second Edition pp. 79-85. The base system supplies typed schemas and provenance only; licensed packages may register actual catalogs.
Advancement strategy
Select exactly one automated Second Edition advancement module: Experience Points, Milestone rewards, or GM-approved Narrative arcs (Second Edition pp. 86-93).

D6E2.Settings.TyfusiusHomebrew.Options.t: Declare an ordered action queue, resolve it in initiative segments, and calculate movement from each character's own queue and MAP.
At the start of the round, each character declares every intended action in order. Link actions to Skills, Attributes, weapons, or Running whenever they use a dice pool. Foundry applies that character's own MAP and uses the lowest linked post-MAP pool to find segment movement: count its full dice, then cap that distance at Move divided by declared actions. Every normal segment permits that movement. A Running action rolls against Difficulty 5 per declared action and doubles the segment distance on success. Failure spends Running and its MAP but gives only normal movement. A Wild Die 1 resolved as a Complication removes every other action and leaves only one normal segment movement total. Reactive movement spends the reactor's own next action, uses the reactor's own queue and MAP, and never triggers another movement reaction.

Kael has Move 12 and declares three linked actions. His lowest pool after his 2D MAP is 3D, so he may move 3 meters in each segment: the dice allow 3 meters and the Move cap is 12 ÷ 3 = 4. If Running is his current action, Difficulty is 3 × 5 = 15 and success raises that segment to 6 meters. A guard who declared only two actions calculates movement from the guard's own pools and Move ÷ 2; the guard may therefore react farther than Kael even though the reaction happens during Kael's segment.
D6E2.Settings.TyfusiusHomebrew.Options.t: Shift every thrown-explosive range boundary by one meter for each Strength pip above or below 2D. No boundary can fall below zero.
A printed grenade range assumes Strength 2D. Strength 3D has three extra pips, so every boundary moves 3 meters farther. Strength 1D has three fewer pips, so every boundary moves 3 meters closer. Mark a Weapon as Thrown explosive and enter its printed Short start, Short end, Medium end, and Long end.
Printed ranges 3–4 / 7 / 12 become 6–7 / 10 / 15 at Strength 3D. At Strength 1D they become 0–1 / 4 / 9; Point Blank is empty and a throw at 0 meters counts as Short.
D6E2.Settings.TyfusiusHomebrew.Options.t: Shift every thrown-explosive range boundary by one meter for each effective Brawn pip above or below 2D. No boundary can fall below zero.

D6E2.Settings.TyfusiusHomebrew.CombinedA: Start beside an Attribute or Skill in the GM Quickbar. Every participant agrees, then the highest Command leader (or Perception when untrained) rolls against the GM's difficulty. A leader who also works takes −1D. The highest task pool receives the final bonus.

Three participants provide +1D; four provide +1D+1; five provide +1D+2; and eight provide +2D+2. Each point missed on Command removes 1D, never below zero. Combat may split the bonus between attack and damage; other multi-Skill tasks may divide it between checks.

Track a separate 1–3 point identity pool, Suspicion, exposure, clearing a name, and going public (pp. 208–211).
Use Superpowers
Enable custom and contributed ranked Superpower Talents, their separate creation budget, and generic enhancement and limitation accounting (pp. 212–226). Requires Perks, Flaws & Talents.
Use Gadgets & Gear
Enable superheroic Gear Items that grant a narrow +1D gadget roll or contain one or more Superpower Talents (pp. 227–228). Requires Superpowers.
Use Hidden Bases & Hideouts
Enable standalone Hideout Actors with location, group membership, feature accounting, and relocation timing (pp. 229–234). Requires Perks, Flaws & Talents.
Use Nemesis, Companions & Sidekicks
Enable protected Nemesis encounter pools and experience matching, Companion recovery, and half-budget Sidekick creation (pp. 235–237). Requires Perks, Flaws & Talents.
Superpower campaign level
Choose how many dice each new hero may spend on Superpower Talents. This setting is used only while Superpowers are enabled (p. 212).

D6E2.Superheroic.Help: Use these cards only for the superheroic foundation modules enabled by your GM.
D6E2.Superheroic.SkillsHelp: Flying lets you move by its whole dice and can replace Agility for Dodge without counting Agility twice. Gambling and Streetwise cover chance-taking and underworld knowledge; the GM decides their exact results.
D6E2.Superheroic.HeroPointsHelp: These choices extend the campaign's normal Hero Point method. Each choice costs one point.
D6E2.Superheroic.ExtraActionAudit: One action was added to the declared queue without increasing the Multiple Action Penalty.
D6E2.Superheroic.TalentRequired: Add a Talent to this Character before using this option.
D6E2.Superheroic.BoostTalentAudit: {name} counts as rank {boosted} instead of rank {rank} for this use.
D6E2.Superheroic.NoEligibleAlly: No other owned Character is available to receive a Hero Point.
D6E2.Superheroic.ExplainAction: In combat, spend one point after declaring actions to add one action that does not increase MAP.
D6E2.Superheroic.ExplainTalent: Spend one point when using a Talent so it counts as one rank higher. Superpower Talents use the same rule when that module is enabled.
D6E2.Superheroic.ExplainTransfer: Give one point to an ally who currently has fewer than three.
D6E2.Superheroic.ExplainCap: On a capped roll, choose Ignore cap in the roll dialog instead of another Hero Point use.
D6E2.Superheroic.DieCodeCapHelp: The cap applies after bonuses and preserves legal +1 or +2 pips. Only Character Actors are capped; opponents and GM-controlled villain types remain uncapped.
D6E2.Superheroic.BypassCapHelp: Spend 1 Hero Point to ignore the {cap}D cap for this roll.
D6E2.Superheroic.SecretIdentityHelp: This private pool is separate from ordinary Hero Points and begins at 1.
D6E2.Superheroic.SpendIdentityPointAudit: One Secret Identity Hero Point was spent for a narratively justified benefit.
D6E2.Superheroic.ReinforceAudit: Active roleplaying reinforced the Secret Identity and awarded one point.
D6E2.Superheroic.GoPublicAudit: The Secret Identity was permanently abandoned; its private point pool is no longer available.
D6E2.Superheroic.ExplainIdentityPool: The GM may award one identity point when the secret life plays a prominent active role, to a maximum of three.
D6E2.Superheroic.ExplainSuspicion: Whenever Suspicion rises, Foundry rolls 1d6 openly. If the die is equal to or below the new Suspicion, the identity is Exposed.
D6E2.Superheroic.ExplainExposure: An Exposed hero cannot use the identity pool. The GM may clear the name after an adventure or mark the identity permanently public.
D6E2.Superheroic.SuspicionExposedAudit: Suspicion {suspicion}; rolled {roll}. The Secret Identity is Exposed.
D6E2.Superheroic.SuspicionSafeAudit: Suspicion {suspicion}; rolled {roll}. The Secret Identity remains safe.
D6E2.Superheroic.OwnerRequired: You must own this Character to use that superheroic action.
D6E2.Superheroic.TargetOwnerRequired: A player may only give a Hero Point to another Character they own; a GM can complete other transfers.
D6E2.Superheroic.AllyRequired: Choose another Character as the ally.
D6E2.Superheroic.TargetBelowThreeRequire: The ally must have fewer than 3 Hero Points.
D6E2.Superheroic.GMRequired: Only the GM may approve that Secret Identity change.
D6E2.Superheroic.ModuleRequired: Enable the required superheroic module first.
D6E2.Superheroic.ActionDeclarationRequir: Declare this character's actions before buying an extra action.
D6E2.Superheroic.SecretIdentityUnavailab: The Secret Identity pool is unavailable while exposed or public.
D6E2.Superheroic.SecretIdentityPointRequ: No Secret Identity Hero Point is available to spend.
D6E2.Superheroic.SecretIdentityPointMaxi: The Secret Identity Hero Point pool is already at its maximum of 3.
D6E2.Superheroic.SecretIdentityNotExpose: Only an exposed Secret Identity needs its name cleared.
D6E2.Superpowers.Title: Superpowers
D6E2.Superpowers.Help: Superpowers are ranked Talents paid from their own campaign budget.
D6E2.Superpowers.CustomBoundary: Create a Talent, give it your own lawful name and description, then mark it as a Superpower on its Item sheet. Public D6 System Second Edition intentionally includes no protected printed power, enhancement, or limitation catalog.
D6E2.Superpowers.MarkTalentHelp: Superpower Talents use the campaign's separate Superpower dice instead of ordinary creation Skill dice.
D6E2.Superpowers.EnhancementCostHelp: Add the generic cost of your lawful custom or contributed enhancements. This amount is paid again at every rank.
D6E2.Superpowers.LimitationCreditHelp: Subtract the generic credit once from the whole Talent, not once per rank. Final cost can never drop below 1D.
D6E2.Superpowers.ModuleInactive: The Talent may be prepared now, but its Superpower budget and use controls remain inactive until the GM enables Superpowers.
D6E2.Superpowers.None: No custom or contributed Superpower Talents are on this Character yet.
D6E2.Superpowers.RelianceAudit: The player declared reliance on this non-automatic Superpower Talent for the current action or result.
D6E2.Superpowers.TalentRequired: Choose a Superpower Talent on this Character.
D6E2.Superpowers.ExplainBudget: The number beside Superpowers shows dice spent compared with this campaign's starting power budget.
D6E2.Superpowers.ExplainRanks: A ranked power pays its base cost once for every rank. Skills granted by a power improve as normal Skills; they do not rise automatically with the power's rank.
D6E2.Superpowers.ExplainModifiers: Enhancement cost repeats at every rank. Limitation credit is subtracted once from the final total, which can never be less than 1D.
D6E2.Superpowers.ExplainReliance: Automatic powers need no declaration. For another power, click Rely on power when its benefit matters; this records the declaration without consuming an extra action unless that custom power says otherwise.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Title: Gadgets & Gear
D6E2.GadgetsGear.ItemHelp: Use Gadget for a narrow +1D situational bonus. Use Gear when the item contains one or more Superpower Talents.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.CharacterHelp: Use equipped superheroic equipment, review contained powers, and track malfunction, repair, destruction, and rebuilding.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.ModuleInactive: You may prepare this Item now, but its use controls remain unavailable until the GM enables Gadgets & Gear and its Superpowers dependency.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Kind.Label: Superheroic equipment type
D6E2.GadgetsGear.State.Label: Condition
D6E2.GadgetsGear.UseCaseHelp: Keep this narrow: a Gadget normally adds +1D to one particular use, not every roll with that Attribute or Skill.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.NoSuperpowers: No custom or contributed Superpower Talents are available in this item.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.RebuildDisabled: A contributed limitation replaces the normal rebuilding rule
D6E2.GadgetsGear.NoNormalRebuild: Normal rebuilding is unavailable; follow the contributed limitation instead.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Malfunctioned: A Complication caused the item to malfunction; it must be repaired before it can be used again.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Repaired: The item was repaired and is ready to use.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Rebuilt: The destroyed item was rebuilt and is ready to use.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.PowerUseAudit: The player declared use of a Superpower Talent contained in this piece of Gear.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.None: No configured Gadgets or Superpower Gear are on this Character yet.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.ExplainGadget: A Gadget adds exactly +1D to its configured narrow Attribute or Skill use. The roll card records the item and use case.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.ExplainGear: Gear may contain several Superpower Talents. If another character uses a copied or transferred item, its declarations record the −1D borrower penalty.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.ExplainState: A Gadget Complication automatically marks it malfunctioning. The GM can record Gear complications, repairs, destruction, and the source-derived rebuild time.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.ExampleGadget: Example: configure a climbing tool for Athletics when climbing. Use gadget rolls Athletics at +1D, but it gives no bonus to jumping or other Athletics uses.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.ExampleGear: Example: link two lawful custom Superpower Talents to one piece of Gear. Foundry shows both powers and adds their costs when it calculates normal rebuild time.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Error.OwnerRequired: You must own this Character to use its superheroic equipment.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Error.GMRequired: Only a Gamemaster may change superheroic equipment condition.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Error.ModuleRequired: Gadgets & Gear must be enabled with its Superpowers dependency.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Error.GadgetRequired: Choose a configured Gadget on this Character.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Error.GearRequired: Choose configured Superpower Gear on this Character.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Error.EquippedRequired: Equip the item before using it.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Error.ReadyRequired: Repair or rebuild the item before using it.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Error.TargetRequired: The Gadget roll must use its configured Attribute or Skill.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Error.UseCaseRequired: Describe the narrow situation in which this Gadget grants +1D.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Error.PowerRequired: Choose a Superpower Talent contained in this Gear.
D6E2.GadgetsGear.Error.RebuildDisabled: This item's contributed limitation replaces the normal rebuilding rule.
D6E2.Hideout.Title: Hidden Base or Hideout
D6E2.Hideout.BasicSupplies: Living quarters and basic supplies are always included.
D6E2.Hideout.FeaturesHelp: A new hideout normally has four features. The GM may change that allowance. Features beyond the allowance remain visible for table review.
D6E2.Hideout.CatalogHelp: Choose a feature supplied by a lawful companion or private content module.
D6E2.Hideout.NoCatalogFeatures: No contributed hideout features are currently available. Add a custom feature instead.
D6E2.Hideout.NoFeatures: No features have been selected yet.
D6E2.Hideout.MissingPrerequisite: Add the required feature or features first: {ids}.
D6E2.Hideout.NotRepeatable: That contributed feature cannot be selected more than once.
D6E2.Hideout.NoMemberCandidates: No accessible character is available to add.
D6E2.Hideout.OwnershipHelp: This roster records which characters share the hideout. Use Foundry's Ownership configuration to grant the matching players access to the Hideout Actor.
D6E2.Hideout.RelocationHelp: Relocating or re-establishing a hideout normally takes one game month per selected feature. Enter an override only when the GM's fiction or adventure changes that time.
D6E2.Hideout.InactiveHelp: The data remains visible, but editing is disabled until the GM enables this rules component and Perks, Flaws & Talents.
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.Title: Nemesis, Companions & Sidekicks
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.Help: The GM configures these optional relationships. Foundry handles the numeric parts while the table decides the fiction.
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.NemesisHel: A Nemesis is built as a normal campaign character. At the start of each encounter, the GM rolls a fresh pool of 1d6 + 3 Nemesis Points; those points work through the ordinary Hero Point controls.
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.BeginEncou: The fresh encounter pool contains {points} Nemesis Points.
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.ResolveNem: GM: record defeat and award hero
{hero} drove away or defeated the Nemesis and recovered 1 Hero Point.
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.CompanionH: Record one important person, creature, or touchstone. Meaningful time together can recover 1 Hero Point when the table agrees.
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.RecoverCom: Meaningful time with {name} recovered 1 Hero Point.
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.SidekickHe: A Sidekick starts with half the ordinary Attribute, Skill, and Superpower dice. The GM must confirm the printed character and mentor requirements on p. 236; protected Feature names and text are not distributed here.
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.SidekickCr: Use half starting-dice budgets during creation
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.Requiremen: GM confirms the Sidekick and mentor requirements from p. 236
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.ExampleNem: Example: the GM rolls 4, so this encounter begins with 7 Nemesis Points. A later encounter replaces that pool with a new roll.
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.ExampleCom: Example: after a difficult mission, a hero spends a meaningful scene with their trusted companion and recovers 1 Hero Point.
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.ExampleSid: Example: a normal 12D Attribute budget becomes 6D, a normal 7D Skill budget becomes 3D, and an odd Superpower budget is rounded down to whole dice.
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.Safety: Sidekick stories—especially stories involving young people or danger—need the whole table's consent. The GM may remove the relationship if it becomes unsafe or disruptive.
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.NemesisReq: Mark this Character as an active Nemesis first.
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.LinkedHero: Choose a valid linked hero before recording the outcome.
D6E2.SuperheroicRelationships.CompanionR: Record a companion or touchstone first.
